title: Indices, Logarithm and Surds Quiz 8
description: Different bases: take logarithms of both sides.
instructions: Indices, Logarithm and Surds: Exponential equations with logarithms.
Write maths answers with the keypad. Any equal form is accepted.
Every question has a trap. Slow down at the signs.

questions.question: Solve $7^{x}=9$. Give an exact answer.
questions.explanation: Take logs: $x\ln7=\ln9$, so $x=\dfrac{\ln9}{\ln7}$. Watch out: the logs are divided, not subtracted.

questions.question: Solve $e^{t+6}=2$, giving $t$ to 3 decimal places.
questions.explanation: Take $\ln$: $t+6=\ln2$, so $t=\ln2-6\approx-5.307$. Watch out: $\ln2$ is about $0.693$, and we then subtract $6$.

questions.question: Solve $10^{5-x}=8$, giving $x$ to 3 decimal places.
questions.explanation: $5-x=\log8\approx0.903$, so $x=5-\log8\approx4.097$. Watch out: it is $5-\log 8$, not $\log 8-5$.

questions.question: Solve $5e^{2z+4}-8=0$. Give an exact answer.
questions.explanation: $e^{2z+4}=\dfrac85$, so $2z+4=\ln\dfrac85$ and $z=\dfrac{\ln(8/5)-4}{2}$. Watch out: divide by $5$ **before** taking logs.

questions.question: Solve $2^{4y+1}-3^{y}=0$, giving $y$ to 3 decimal places.
questions.explanation: $2^{4y+1}=3^y$ gives $(4y+1)\ln2=y\ln3$, so $y=\dfrac{-\ln2}{4\ln2-\ln3}\approx-0.414$. Watch out: $y$ is negative, so check the sign.

questions.question: Solve $3^{x}=20$. Which is the solution?
questions.explanation: $x\ln3=\ln20$, so $x=\dfrac{\ln20}{\ln3}$. Watch out: $\ln20-\ln3$ equals $\ln\dfrac{20}{3}$, which is not the same.

questions.question: $\ln(5^{x})=5\ln x$.
questions.explanation: The power rule gives $\ln(5^x)=x\ln5$. Watch out: the exponent $x$ comes down, but the base stays $5$.

questions.question: Solve $7^{x}=9$. One step is wrong. Tap it.
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by $\ln7$: $x=\dfrac{\ln9}{\ln7}$. Watch out: $\ln 7$ multiplies $x$, so it is divided, not subtracted.

questions.question: Find $\ln e^{3}+e^{\ln2}$.
questions.explanation: $\ln e^3=3$ and $e^{\ln2}=2$, so the sum is $5$. Watch out: $e^{\ln 2}$ equals $2$, because the functions undo each other.

questions.question: Solve $e^{2x}=5$. Give an exact answer.
questions.explanation: $2x=\ln5$, so $x=\dfrac{\ln5}{2}$. Watch out: the $2$ divides the whole logarithm.
